nodes.summary: For every formula $\varphi$, $\mathrm{GL} \vdash \Box\varphi \to \Box\Box\varphi$.
nodes.title: GL proves axiom 4

nodes.summary: For a modal formula $\varphi$, Löb's axiom is Read with $\Box$ as provability in Peano arithmetic, it is the formalized Löb theorem $\mathrm{PA} \vdash \mathrm{Prov}(\ulcorner \mathrm{Prov}(\ulcorner\varphi\urcorner) \to \varphi\urcorner) \to \mathrm{Prov}(\ulcorner\varphi\urcorner)$.
nodes.title: Löb's axiom

nodes.summary: A formula $\varphi$ is a theorem of GL if and only if $\varphi$ is valid in every Kripke model on a finite set of worlds whose accessibility relation is transitive and irreflexive (Segerberg 1971; independently de Jongh and Kripke). Completeness even holds for finite transitive irreflexive trees; the Lean statement uses the larger class of finite strict partial orders, so it is the weaker completeness claim.
nodes.title: Completeness of GL for finite strict partial orders

nodes.title: The de Jongh–Sambin fixed point for one boxed occurrence

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be modalised in $A$. There is a formula $H$ in which $p$ does not occur, all of whose atoms occur in $A$, such that $\mathrm{GL} \vdash H \leftrightarrow A(H)$.
nodes.title: The de Jongh–Sambin fixed point theorem

For all formulas $\psi$ and $\chi$, (\psi \leftrightarrow \chi),$$ where $\boxdot\theta$ abbreviates $\theta \wedge \Box\theta$; the Lean statement spells out the four hypotheses as curried implications. In particular two fixed points of $A$ are GL-provably equivalent: if $\mathrm{GL} \vdash \psi \leftrightarrow A(\psi)$ and…
nodes.title: Uniqueness of fixed points in GL

nodes.summary: In a Hilbert–Bernays–Löb provability structure, suppose that for every sentence $A$ there is a sentence $B$ with $T \vdash B \to (\mathrm{Prov}(B) \to A)$ and $T \vdash (\mathrm{Prov}(B) \to A) \to B$ (the diagonal lemma for $\mathrm{Prov}(x) \to A$). Then for every $A$,
nodes.title: Formalized Löb theorem

nodes.summary: Let $W$ be a nonempty set of worlds, $R$ a relation on $W$, and assume there is at least one atom. Löb's axiom $\Box(\Box\varphi \to \varphi) \to \Box\varphi$ holds at every world of every model on the frame $(W, R)$, for every formula $\varphi$, if and only if $R$ is transitive and conversely well-founded.
nodes.title: Frame correspondence for Löb's axiom

nodes.summary: If $\mathrm{K4} \vdash \varphi$ then $\mathrm{GL} \vdash \varphi$.
nodes.title: Every theorem of K4 is a theorem of GL

nodes.summary: The provability logic GL (also written L, KW or PrL) is the normal modal logic $\mathrm{K} \oplus \text{Löb}$: its extra axioms are the instances $\Box(\Box\varphi \to \varphi) \to \Box\varphi$ of Löb's axiom for all formulas $\varphi$, and its theorems are closed under modus ponens and necessitation.
nodes.title: Extra axioms of the provability logic GL

nodes.summary: Read arithmetically: if PA is consistent, PA does not prove its own consistency statement $\neg\mathrm{Prov}(\ulcorner\bot\urcorner)$.
nodes.title: Modal Gödel's second incompleteness theorem

eg\Box

eg\Box ot .$$ Arithmetically, by the uniqueness of fixed points, the sentences asserting their own unprovability are exactly those PA-provably equivalent to $\mathrm{Con}(\mathrm{PA})$.
nodes.title: The Gödel sentence of GL

nodes.title: Hilbert–Bernays–Löb provability structure

nodes.summary: The Kripke model with one world that sees no world, every atom false. Its relation is empty, hence transitive and conversely well-founded; there $\Box\psi$ holds vacuously for every $\psi$.
nodes.title: The one-world irreflexive Kripke model

nodes.summary: In a Hilbert–Bernays–Löb provability structure with the diagonal property of the formalized Löb theorem, if $T \vdash \mathrm{Prov}(A) \to A$ then $T \vdash A$. With $A = \bot$: if $T$ proves its consistency statement $\neg\mathrm{Prov}(\bot)$, then $T \vdash \bot$ (Gödel's second incompleteness theorem).
nodes.title: Löb's theorem

nodes.summary: An atom $p$ is modalised in a formula $A$ when every occurrence of $p$ in $A$ lies in the scope of some $\Box$. For example $p$ is modalised in $\neg\Box p$ and in $\Box(p \to q)$, but not in $p \to \Box p$. This is the hypothesis of the de Jongh–Sambin fixed point theorem.
nodes.title: Atom occurring only under a box

nodes.summary: If $\varphi \to \psi$ is a theorem of K and $\varphi$ is a theorem of a normal modal logic $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then $\psi$ is a theorem of $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Modus ponens with a K theorem

nodes.summary: If $\varphi \to \psi$ is a theorem of K4 and $\varphi$ is a theorem of GL, then $\psi$ is a theorem of GL.
nodes.title: Modus ponens with a K4 theorem in GL

nodes.summary: $\mathrm{K4} \nvdash \Box(\Box\bot \to \bot) \to \Box\bot$. Hence GL strictly extends K4.
nodes.title: K4 does not prove Löb's axiom

nodes.summary: $\mathrm{GL} \nvdash \Box\bot \to \bot$. Hence GL does not contain the logic T. Moreover no consistent extension of GL closed under necessitation proves $\Box\bot \to \bot$: necessitation and Löb's axiom would give $\Box\bot$ and then $\bot$. (Solovay's logic GLS, which adds all instances of $\Box\psi \to \psi$ to GL, is closed under modus ponens only.)
nodes.title: GL does not prove reflection for `⊥`

nodes.summary: $\mathrm{GL} \nvdash \bot$.
nodes.title: Consistency of GL

nodes.summary: Given a Hilbert–Bernays–Löb provability structure and a sentence $f(p)$ for each atom $p$, the realization $f^*$ sends $p$ to $f(p)$, $\bot$ to falsity, $\varphi \to \psi$ to $f^*(\varphi) \to f^*(\psi)$ and $\Box\varphi$ to $\mathrm{Prov}(f^*(\varphi))$.
nodes.title: Arithmetical realization of a modal formula

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be modalised in $\varphi$, let $M$ be a Kripke model and $w$ a world, and let $U$ be a set of worlds closed under the relation and containing every successor of $w$. If two sets of worlds $S$ and $S'$ agree on $U$, then $M[p \mapsto S], w \models \varphi \iff M[p \mapsto S'], w \models \varphi$.
nodes.title: A modalised atom is read only at visible worlds

nodes.summary: In a Hilbert–Bernays–Löb provability structure with the diagonal property of the formalized Löb theorem, if $\mathrm{GL} \vdash \varphi$ then $T \vdash f^*(\varphi)$ for every realization $f$.
nodes.title: Arithmetical soundness of GL

nodes.summary: In a Hilbert–Bernays–Löb provability structure, $T \vdash f^*(\varphi)$ for every theorem $\varphi$ of K4 and every realization $f$: axiom 4 is realized by D3.
nodes.title: Realizations of K4 theorems are theorems

nodes.summary: In a Hilbert–Bernays–Löb provability structure, if $T \vdash f^*(\psi)$ for every extra axiom $\psi$ of $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then $T \vdash f^*(\varphi)$ for every theorem $\varphi$ of $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Realizations of theorems of a normal modal logic are theorems

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model whose accessibility relation $R$ is transitive and conversely well-founded: there is no infinite chain $w_0 \mathrel{R} w_1 \mathrel{R} w_2 \mathrel{R} \cdots$. Then $\Box(\Box\varphi \to \varphi) \to \Box\varphi$ holds at every world of $M$, for every formula $\varphi$. A conversely well-founded relation is irreflexive.
nodes.title: Löb's axiom is valid on transitive conversely well-founded frames

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model with finitely many worlds whose accessibility relation is transitive and irreflexive. Every theorem of GL is valid in $M$.
nodes.title: Soundness of GL for finite strict partial orders

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model whose accessibility relation is transitive and conversely well-founded. Every theorem of GL is valid in $M$.
nodes.title: Soundness of GL
Logic

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
